lines.text: Insurance [verzekering] helps you when you get into trouble, for example if there is a fire in your house.
Health insurance [zorgverzekering] — insurance against healthcare costs [zorgkosten] — is mandatory [verplicht].
You can choose from many insurance companies.
When you take out [afsluit] an insurance, you get a policy [polis] — a kind of contract.
You pay money for an insurance: the premium [premie].
Personal liability insurance [AVP, aansprakelijkheidsverzekering voor particulieren]: if you or your child accidentally [per ongeluk] breaks something belonging to someone else, the AVP pays.
Not for your own belongings.
An AVP is not mandatory [niet verplicht], but without an AVP you have to pay a lot of money if something is broken.
Home contents insurance [inboedelverzekering]: your household contents [inboedel] is everything in and around your house.
You get money for damage [schade] to your belongings caused by fire, water, a small accident, or if things are stolen.
Not mandatory.
Buildings insurance [opstalverzekering, also known as woonhuisverzekering]: required by the bank if you take out a mortgage [hypotheek] on your own home.
It pays if something on your house breaks, for example your roof due to fire, storm or water.
Statutory liability insurance [WA-verzekering, wettelijke aansprakelijkheid] is mandatory for a vehicle [voertuig]: car, motorcycle or moped.
If you cause damage to someone else, this insurance pays.
Insurance for damage to your own vehicle or against theft is not mandatory.
For a motor vehicle you must also pay tax [belasting].

Other, non-mandatory insurances: travel insurance [reisverzekering] — for example your suitcase is stolen — and funeral insurance [uitvaartverzekering] for the costs of a burial [begrafenis] or cremation [crematie].
If you have damage, you must report [melden] it quickly to the insurance company, via internet or telephone.
You fill in a form.
The insurance only pays if something broke by accident, not if it is your own fault.
Sometimes they ask for extra proof, for example a receipt [kassabon].
